dedupe_keys.name: texbat texas spoofing test battery of recorded gps spoofing scenarios version 1 1

description: TEXBAT is a battery of recorded GPS spoofing scenarios for evaluating civil GPS signal authentication techniques, from the Radionavigation Laboratory at the University of Texas at Austin. It was described at ION GNSS 2012 as the data component of an evolving standard for spoof resistance of commercial receivers. Version 1.1 includes the original datasets of version 1.0 and two new datasets, ds7 and ds8. Each scenario is a recording of raw radio-frequency samples of the GPS L1 band, in static and dynamic settings, with spoofing attacks of different power and synchronisation, such as time push and position push; a later analysis of the datasets with a high-fidelity software receiver was published in 2016. Coverage: recordings made in Texas, a set of scenarios. Format and access: binary sample files (.bin) downloadable from the university, free. Caveats: spoofing was injected in recordings, not broadcast over the air; GPS L1 only; files are large; the scenario list should be read from the papers. Simulation uses: benchmark signals for testing the resilience of GNSS receivers used in timing for telecom and power networks. Related records: data-oakbat-gnss-spoofing-interference-test-battery is a newer battery of the same kind; data-fgi-gnss-jamming-spoofing-dataset-repository gives jamming and spoofing recordings; model-fgi-gsrx is a software receiver to process them.
